display.behavior: Preserve readable content, semantics and host layout; decorative content must not intercept input.

action.behavior: Use native activation, accessible names, visible focus and explicit button type. Host owns success and side effects.

field.behavior: Keep labels, refs, native names/autofill and event contracts. Do not silently switch controlledness.

overlay.behavior: Restore focus, scope portals, coordinate Escape/outside dismissal and make closed content non-interactive. Do not bypass an outer focus trap.

selection.behavior: Reflect controlled values truthfully. Keyboard input is immediate; preserve pointer motion and resize alignment.

feedback.behavior: Use truthful labels; retain host data/drafts on failure. Cancel owned timers and animation frames on unmount.

layout.behavior: Use semantic spacing and allow content growth; avoid layout changes outside the adopted scope.

effect.behavior: Keep decorative layers bounded and pointer-transparent. Preserve artwork and readable foreground content.

helper.behavior: Keep helpers side-effect free during render and do not introduce application infrastructure.

inherited.rule: Consume semantic tokens; appearance inherits from HighwayTheme.

glass.rule: Preserve translucent wash, rim, inset highlight, bounded blur and layered elevation; use the opaque accessibility fallback.

field.rule: Preserve control geometry, contrast, invalid/focus distinctions and phone input minimums.

opaque-overlay.rule: Preserve the component’s authored overlay material and scoped portal tokens. Native menus/dialogs stay opaque; ProfileMenu and WorkspaceSwitcher retain their translucent blurred surfaces. Do not apply one background to every menu.

component-surface.rule: Use Highway surface and hairline shadow tokens; do not substitute for GlassCard.

decorative.rule: Bound effect layers and preserve prefixed blur masks.

none.policy: Do not add animation without a communication purpose.

press.policy: Preserve existing press geometry and focus. Reduced motion removes spatial feedback.

overlay.purpose: Anchor a transient surface to its trigger.
overlay.policy: Preserve component-owned entrance/exit recipes: Floating scale/slide enters at 300ms with 200ms opacity, exits at 150ms with 120ms opacity. Keep correct origins, retargetable transitions, reduced motion, and inert closed content.

selection.purpose: Connect pointer selection to the active indicator.
selection.policy: Preserve each selection recipe: Tabs uses its 300ms emphasized travel; SegmentedControl retains 250ms travel. Keyboard and reduced-motion paths are immediate; measurements respond to resizing and wrapping.

slider.purpose: Quick pointer clicks settle with the original spring; sustained dragging tracks directly.
slider.policy: 250ms spring, 80ms drag threshold; keyboard and reduced motion instant.

expansion.purpose: Reveal related content without abruptly changing its container.
expansion.policy: 350ms height, 250ms content with 100ms entrance delay, 150ms content exit; interruptions retarget; hidden content inert.

inherited-specialty.purpose: Preserve a distinct existing choreography until individually reviewed.
inherited-specialty.policy: Do not normalize all timings. Any change requires explicit visual comparison, reduced-motion coverage and lifecycle cleanup.

number-roll.purpose: Show numeric value changes with directional digit rolls while separators remain still.
number-roll.policy: Default 900ms roll with configurable duration and initial delay; begin when visible, preserve digit identity, cancel frames and timers on unmount, and resolve immediately under reduced motion.

copy-feedback.purpose: Confirm a successful clipboard write without shifting the control or surrounding content.
copy-feedback.policy: Keep idle and success labels in shared grid space. Preserve the 160ms opacity and 220ms vertical transition, announce clipboard failures, reset feedback after 2 seconds, and remove spatial transitions under reduced motion.

policy: Highway canonical packages are the single source of truth for showcase, docs, MCP and consumers. Preserve authored component geometry, materials, emphasis and distinct motion; shared tokens are not permission for blanket visual overrides. Contracts are review requirements, not certification of every state.
